labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is ELISA, which needs a flat plate or a deep-well plate as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt (slot 1, load name nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt), which is a PCR plate or PCR strips. A plate reader reads a flat, clear-bottomed plate, and an ELISA plate is coated before the samples arrive; a PCR plate is neither coated nor readable, and its thin-walled conical wells hold little and are meant for a thermocycler. The plate map checks what each well holds, not what plate it is.
labware.fix: Load a flat plate (corning_96_wellplate_360ul_flat or nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat) as the destination: it is what a plate reader reads and what an assay or a culture is done in.

protocol.py: 4 biology problems (1 error, 1 warning, 2 notes).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 6 stocks
   line 60:  p300.aspirate(250, source_plate[f"A{i-1}"])
   At line 60 the tip went into serum 1 (well A1 in slot 4), serum 2 (well A2 in slot 4),
   serum 3 (well A3 in slot 4), serum 4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 2 more while it still
   carried diluent (tube A2 in slot 2), serum 2 (well A2 in slot 4), serum 3 (well A3 in
   slot 4), serum 4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 3 more from an earlier step (this line did it 6
   times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from
   them then took the unwanted material along into 24 other wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5,
   A6, A7, A8 and 16 more in slot 1.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4.
   Also reached 24 other wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 16 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 60 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [8811abe0d365]

2. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: standard (tube A1 in slot 2)
   line 48:  p300.aspirate(250, tuberack["A1"])
   At line 48 the tip went into standard (tube A1 in slot 2) while it still carried serum 1
   (well A1 in slot 4) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a
   little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does
   not belong there. The protocol does not draw from it again, so this run is not harmed,
